paragraphs.text: Many cities are replacing diesel buses with electric ones. Electric buses are quieter and produce no exhaust fumes in the street, which improves air quality where people walk and wait.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The main drawback has been range. Early models could travel only about 150 kilometres before recharging, which was not enough for a full day’s service. Newer buses carry larger batteries, but these are heavy and reduce the number of passengers the bus can carry.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Some cities avoid large batteries by charging buses briefly at the end of each route, using equipment mounted above the bus stop. A few minutes of charging is enough for the next journey.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Although electric buses cost more to buy, operators report that they are cheaper to run, because electricity costs less than diesel and the motors need less maintenance.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Several manufacturers now offer buses that can be fitted with extra batteries for longer journeys, so operators can choose the design that suits each part of the city.
paragraphs.label: E
